draft.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander views of health
card: Many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples see health as holistic. This means the whole of life is considered together, not the body alone.
Health links a person to family, community, culture, Country and spirit. Country includes land, waters and sky, and the bonds people have with them.
Because these parts are connected, harm to one can affect a person's wellbeing. For example, being cut off from Country or community can affect how well a person feels.
This view differs from a definition that looks only at whether a person has a disease. Views and experiences differ between communities and people.
draft.remember: Health is holistic: the person is linked to family, community, culture, Country and spirit.

a.q: What does it mean to say that many Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples see health as holistic?
opts: A person's health is linked to family, culture and Country
A person's health depends on their body being free of illness
A person's health is judged by the doctor, not the community
A person's health is set by their age and stage of life
a.why: A holistic view considers the whole of life together, including family, community, culture, Country and spirit. The option about the body being free of illness describes a narrower view that looks only at disease.
a.clue: Holistic means the whole, not one part.

b.q: Jarrah, a young man from Victoria, moves to a city for work and is away from his family and Country. He feels unwell although a check-up finds no illness. Which reason best fits a holistic view of health?
opts: Being apart from family and Country can affect his wellbeing
A clear check-up means that his health must be good
His wellbeing is shaped by his body and nothing else
Moving for work always harms the health of young people
b.why: A holistic view links health to family, community and Country, so being apart from them can affect wellbeing even without disease. The clear check-up option is tempting, but it treats health as only the absence of illness.
b.clue: Look beyond the body to what connects Jarrah to others.
